original_question: Can work on the Hitchin fibration and on stringy invariants twisted by mu_n-gerbes be extended to the wild case?
target_in_paper: Problem 10.4 in §10: "Generalize the works [GWZ20], [LW21] on the Hitchin fibration and stringy invariants twisted by μ_n-gerbes to the wild case."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly singles out the same narrow topic as Problem 10.4: extending the Hitchin-fibration/gerbe-twisted stringy-invariant story to the wild setting. It is already much closer to the paper's actual intent than a generic question about wild McKay correspondence or about Hitchin systems in general.
missing_details: The paper states this as a request to generalize two specific works, namely [GWZ20] and [LW21], not just a broad program on Hitchin fibrations.

The nearby explanatory paragraph identifies the precise content to be generalized: [GWZ20] proves the Hausel-Thaddeus topological mirror symmetry conjecture via ℓ-adic integration on Deligne-Mumford stacks, and [LW21] refines that result to the motivic level.
The invariants are not just unspecified 'stringy invariants': the paragraph says the conjecture is formulated in terms of stringy Hodge numbers twisted by μ_n-gerbes.

In this paper, 'wild case' means the paper's standard wild-ramification/wild-stack setting in positive characteristic, not the separate notion of an irregular or 'wild Hitchin system'. The paper's Convention and §2.1 define wildness in terms of positive characteristic and non-tame behavior (allowing stabilizer/group orders divisible by the characteristic).
To make the question stand alone, one should mention the ambient convention that the base field is algebraically closed unless otherwise specified.

The paper does not add extra hypotheses such as a fixed rank, degree, particular group, or a specific form of the Hitchin moduli space in Problem 10.4, so a faithful rewrite should not invent such restrictions.
The author's own gloss on the aim is that one should 'incorporate wild actions into research in this direction'; this interpretive sentence is part of the nearby context and should guide the wording.
refined_question: Can one generalize to the wild setting, over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic and allowing non-tame (wildly ramified/stacky) phenomena, the Groechenig-Wyss-Ziegler and Loeser-Wyss results on the Hitchin fibration—namely, the Hausel-Thaddeus topological mirror symmetry statement formulated via μ_n-gerbe-twisted stringy Hodge numbers and its motivic refinement?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 10.4, and the paper's own wording there is the closest official formulation. The sentence immediately following Problem 10.4 explains exactly which prior results are meant: [GWZ20] proves the Hausel-Thaddeus topological mirror symmetry conjecture by ℓ-adic integration on Deligne-Mumford stacks, and [LW21] refines this to the motivic level; it also specifies that the conjecture is stated using stringy Hodge numbers twisted by μ_n-gerbes. To make the question paper-faithful and stand-alone, the main missing ingredient is the paper's meaning of 'wild': by the Convention and §2.1, wildness is the positive-characteristic, non-tame setting of wild ramification/wild stacky behavior, not the unrelated terminology of 'wild Hitchin systems'. No alternate formulation is given as equivalent in the paper, so none should be added.
